Case studiesServices Engineering practicesTechnologies Industries Company

Home›Engineering Practices
How we build

Modern tools. Unchanged standards.

We use modern AI tools to take the repetitive work off our engineers, so their time goes into architecture, security, and review. The standards don't move. Every line is owned by a person who can explain it.

Book a discovery callRead the FAQ

What AI actually changes

Where it genuinely helps

AI is good at the mechanical middle of the job: setting up services, drafting tests, proposing migrations, writing documentation, and handling large refactors. This is work that used to eat a large part of an engineer's week and rewards speed more than judgment.

Where it changes nothing

It doesn't decide your architecture. It doesn't choose a data model, sign off on a security review, or judge whether a trade-off suits your business. Those calls need context and accountability that no tool carries. Our engineers make them, exactly as they did before.

AI moved the typing. It did not move the thinking, and it never moves the responsibility.

We treat AI tools the way we treat cloud.

We work across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud and choose the one that fits your business, your stack, and your constraints. We don't push a favourite and we don't lock you in. Our view of AI tooling is exactly the same.

Claude CodeCursorGitHub CopilotCodexReplitGeminiWindsurfOllama

Our engineers are hands-on across all of them. Which one we reach for depends on the task, the toolchain you already run, and above all your policy. If your security team has approved some tools and not others, we work inside that list. If they've approved none, that's a supported way of working too.

Most of our work runs through Claude Code, so it's the clearest example to walk through. The guardrails below apply whichever tool is in play.

How we use Claude Code

What it does

  • Sets up services, modules, and boilerplate to our internal patterns
  • Drafts tests, which an engineer then reviews and extends
  • Proposes migrations, which a human approves or rewrites before they run
  • Handles large mechanical refactors, in reviewable steps
  • Writes documentation, runbooks, and API references
  • Explains legacy code, so modernization starts from understanding

What it never does

  • Touch production. Ever.
  • Read production databases or live customer data
  • See secrets, API keys, or .env files, excluded at the tool level
  • Merge its own work, approve a pull request, or skip a review
  • Run destructive commands unattended
  • Make an architecture, schema, or security decision without an engineer owning it

How we keep it safe

Secrets and keys

The risk: The fastest way to leak a credential is to let a tool read a file it never needed.

Secrets live in a manager such as Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or Doppler, never in the repo. AI tools are configured to exclude .env, credential files, and infrastructure directories by design. We prefer short-lived, role-based credentials over static keys, and run secret scanning (gitleaks, TruffleHog) as a pre-commit hook and a CI gate, so a commit carrying a key can't reach the branch.

Database schema and migrations

The risk: A generated migration that looks right and quietly loses data.

Schema is a human decision. An engineer models the data around how it will really be queried and owns that design. A tool may draft a migration; it never runs one. Every migration is versioned, reversible, peer-reviewed, and rehearsed against a copy of the data before it goes near production.

Your data

The risk: Sensitive data ending up somewhere it shouldn't.

Development and testing run on synthetic or masked datasets. Real customer data doesn't enter a developer environment, so it never enters a tool's context. Where a task needs production-shaped data, we generate it, same schema, same edge cases, none of the people.

Code review

The risk: Code nobody actually understands reaching production.

Every change, AI-assisted or not, goes through the same pull request, the same reviewer, and the same standard. An engineer must be able to explain and defend every line they submit. Code nobody can defend does not merge.

The pipeline

The risk: Speed quietly eroding quality over months.

Quality is enforced by machines, not memory. Every commit runs linting, type checking, static analysis, dependency and vulnerability scanning, and the test suite. Coverage thresholds block a merge. Security findings block a merge. The gates are identical whether a human or a tool drafted the change.

Dependencies

The risk: A generated import pulling in an unvetted package.

Dependencies are pinned and lockfiles committed. New packages need review. Automated scanning flags known vulnerabilities on every build, and we produce an SBOM where you need one.

If you'd rather we didn't use AI at all

Some clients work under rules, or preferences, that put AI tooling out of scope. That's a fair position, and we support it in writing rather than by promise.

AI-accelerated

Default

Modern tooling used inside the guardrails above, under enterprise terms with retention disabled. Fastest delivery, standards unchanged.

Restricted context

Scoped

AI tooling allowed but scoped: no proprietary business logic, no regulated code paths, no client repositories in context. Used only on isolated work like tests, docs, and scaffolding.

AI-free

Human-only

No AI tooling touches your codebase. Fully human engineering, guaranteed as a contract addendum, and auditable. We adjust timelines honestly and tell you what the difference is up front.

Whichever tier you choose, the same commitments hold. Your code and data stay inside your boundary or ours as agreed, never in a public tool, never in a consumer account, and never used to train anyone's model. We'll work inside your cloud or VPC where you need it, and sign a DPA that says so.

We're not going to claim a multiple.

The gain shows up in lead time, how long a change takes to go from agreed to live, not in lines of code per day. Setup, tests, migrations, refactors, and documentation move much faster. Architecture, security review, and design decisions take exactly as long as they always did, because rushing those is how projects fail.

The net effect is that our engineers spend far more of their week on the work that actually needs a human. That's where the speed comes from. The standards didn't get lighter, the busywork stopped eating the people who should be thinking.

If going faster meant shipping code nobody understands, we'd go slower. That's not a slogan. It's why the review gate has no exceptions.

What we hold ourselves to

Engineering claims are cheap. These are the measures we track on every engagement and report back to you.

Delivery

Deployment frequency
How often we ship to production. Releases are routine, not events.
Lead time for change
Time from an agreed change to it running in production.
Change failure rate
Share of releases that cause an incident or need a fix.
Time to restore
How fast service is recovered when something does break.

Quality and security

Human-reviewed code
100%
Nothing merges without a named engineer accountable.
Secrets in repo
Zero
Enforced by pre-commit hooks and a CI gate.
Test coverage
Agreed
A threshold agreed with you up front, enforced by the pipeline.
Security scanning
Every build
Known vulnerabilities block the merge.
Prod data in dev
Never
Synthetic or masked datasets only.
Rollback
Every release
Every release ships with a tested way back.

If a measure matters to you and isn't here, tell us and we'll track it.

Engineering FAQ

Does AI write our code?+

It drafts parts of it: setup, tests, migrations, refactors, docs. Every line is then reviewed, and often rewritten, by the engineer who signs their name to it. Nothing merges that a person can't explain.

Could our source code be used to train a model?+

No. We work under enterprise terms with retention disabled and never use consumer AI accounts for client work. If you want that in the contract, we'll put it there.

Do your tools ever see our production data?+

No. Development runs on synthetic or masked data, so real customer records never reach a developer environment.

How are keys and credentials protected?+

They live in a secrets manager, never in the repo. Credential files are excluded from AI tools at the tool level, and scanning blocks any commit carrying a key.

Can we opt out of AI tooling entirely?+

Yes. It's a contractual commitment, not a verbal one, and we'll be straight about what it means for the timeline.

Does moving faster mean lower quality?+

The gates don't change. Coverage, static analysis, scanning, and human review apply to every change however it was drafted.

Can you work inside our cloud, VPC, or on-prem?+

Yes, where your policy needs it.

Who is accountable if something breaks?+

We are. Every change has a named owner, and we stay accountable for how the system performs in the real world.

Want to see the standards before you commit?

We'll walk you through our practices, our AI use policy, and the guardrails in detail. And if you'd rather we didn't use these tools at all, we'll tell you exactly what that changes.

Bonds — AI relationship & wellness platform

An AI platform that helps couples communicate, connect, and grow, with personalised, real-time guidance that adapts to each relationship.

Introduction

Bonds helps people connect, communicate, and grow together, using AI-driven insight tailored to each relationship. It continuously reads user interactions, personality traits, emotional patterns, and engagement to deliver guidance that actually fits the couple in front of it.

Unlike generic wellness apps, Bonds adapts in real time: it anticipates challenges, offers tailored recommendations, and guides users toward meaningful improvement. By combining predictive analytics, sentiment analysis, and dynamic feedback, it gives every user actionable, context-aware support designed to improve communication, deepen connection, and build long-term relationship satisfaction.

The AI doesn't just hand out advice. It learns from behaviour, predicts challenges, and responds in the moment, making relationship wellness smarter, more intuitive, and genuinely personal.

Handling sensitive data

A relationship app holds some of the most personal data a person has. We treated that as a first-order design constraint, not an afterthought. Emotional inputs, messages, voice, and video are encrypted in transit and at rest, personal content is never exposed beyond the user's own account, and the platform is built so guidance can be delivered without compromising privacy or trust.

The personalisation loop

User interactionsmessages, check-ins, activities
AI analysispersonality, emotion, engagement
Personalised guidanceinsights, prompts, recommendations

learns & refines
A continuous cycle — each response feeds back into the analysis, so guidance gets more personal the more a couple uses Bonds.
  • User interactions — everyday messages, check-ins, and shared activities.
  • AI analysis — reads personality, emotional patterns, and engagement.
  • Personalised guidance — insights, prompts, and recommendations tailored to the couple.
  • User acts / responds — the couple acts, and their response feeds the next cycle.

Bonds learns from every interaction, so its guidance gets more personal over time.

Challenges with traditional relationship tools

Generic, one-size-fits-all advice

Traditional tools give everyone the same guidance, ignoring individual personalities, communication styles, and relationship dynamics, so the advice feels irrelevant and users disengage.

Manual, time-consuming tracking

Users have to track their own communication and progress by hand, which is overwhelming for busy couples and rarely sticks.

Inconsistent habit-building

Good habits like showing appreciation or listening well are hard to maintain without personalised, timely reminders.

Hard to measure progress

Without measurable feedback, couples can't tell whether their efforts are actually working, and motivation fades.

No shared, interactive learning

Most tools offer no engaging way for partners to learn and practise skills together, and no secure way to share thoughts and progress.

Shallow tracking

Tools measure surface actions (messages sent, tasks done) but not emotional quality, so users can't see the real health of the relationship.

AI-powered solutions

1

Personalised relationship insights

AI reads behaviour, personality traits, and engagement to deliver tailored guidance on communication, conflict resolution, and emotional support, addressing the unique dynamics of each relationship.

2

AI relationship assistant

A real-time companion that senses emotion and context, then offers conversation starters, prompts for expressing feelings, and next steps to resolve conflict or deepen connection, helping couples communicate better every day.

3

Video guidance & shared learning

AI recommends personalised videos, exercises, and tutorials matched to each couple's style, so partners can learn and practise together, with feedback and progress tracking that turns advice into action.

4

Adaptive feedback & sentiment analysis

Users submit text, voice, or short video, and AI detects stress, mood, tone, and emotional patterns, then responds with actionable tips and prompts to help partners understand each other and resolve conflict.

5

Interactive learning & skill practice

Quizzes, guided activities, and gamified elements (points, levels, badges, daily challenges like “share one appreciation today”) make building communication and empathy skills engaging, while tracking growth over time.

6

Personalised celebration & gift ideas

Bonds remembers key dates (anniversaries, birthdays, milestones) and suggests personalised gifts, date ideas, and messages based on each partner's interests, turning everyday moments into chances to show care.

7

Relationship milestones & goal tracking

Partners track milestones, celebrate achievements, and visualise growth, with feedback on what's improving, what needs attention, and concrete next steps toward shared goals.

Multimodal sentiment analysis

Text
Voice
Short video

Guidance outtips, prompts, real-time feedback

Reading emotion across text, voice, and video, then turning it into useful guidance.

Impact & outcomes

A genuinely personal experience

Tailored insight and timely support make users feel understood, deepening connection and satisfaction.

Engaging shared learning

Interactive, personalised exercises make building relationship skills enjoyable, with tracking and feedback that keep couples practising.

Goal-oriented growth

Couples set and track shared goals, with reminders and suggested activities that turn intention into measurable improvement.

Conflict prevention and resolution

By reading communication and emotional tone, the AI flags potential tension early and suggests ways to defuse it.

Stronger emotional connection

Real-time feedback, prompts, and sentiment analysis support empathy and active listening, building trust and intimacy.

Conclusion

AI and automation are changing how people nurture their relationships, replacing guesswork with personalised, meaningful guidance. Bonds shows how a thoughtful, AI-driven wellness platform can deliver scalable yet deeply personal support across the whole relationship journey. By reading behaviour, personality, and engagement, it lets couples focus on connection while the AI handles personalisation, prediction, and timely guidance, so partners understand each other better, stay engaged, and grow together over time.

Hiremii — AI & automation in recruitment

A cloud-native, multi-tenant hiring platform that uses generative AI, semantic search, and machine learning to streamline the entire recruitment lifecycle.

Introduction

Hiring is being reshaped as AI and automation mature. Traditional recruitment leans on manual work, writing job ads, scanning hundreds of resumes, emailing candidates, tracking applications, which makes it slow and inconsistent. Industry research shows how much room there is to improve: studies of AI-driven recruitment at companies like Unilever, IBM, and Hilton found that AI reduced time-to-hire by up to 85% and recruitment costs by 30%, while improving hiring accuracy and retention. That's the gap our platform was built to close.

Hiremii is a cloud-native, multi-tenant SaaS platform that applies generative AI, semantic search, automation, and machine learning across the whole hiring lifecycle. It automates repetitive work, integrates directly with leading job boards and applicant tracking systems, and uses role-based access control so teams collaborate without compromising data privacy. Its AI engine keeps learning from recruiter decisions to improve candidate-job matching over time.

Note: the percentage figures above come from published industry research, cited as context. They are not results claimed by Ellocent Labs.

Challenges with traditional hiring

1

Manual resume screening is slow and prone to bias

Recruiters spend seconds per resume; one 2024 survey put it at about seven seconds each, so strong candidates get missed. Manual screening also lets unconscious bias creep in, disadvantaging under-represented groups.

2

Writing job ads eats recruiter time

Crafting role descriptions takes hours, and consistency across a team is hard. LinkedIn's 2024 Future of Recruiting report found 57% of recruiters using generative AI say it helps them write job descriptions faster.

3

High application volumes make shortlisting hard

Keyword-matching tools miss context and quality. Modern NLP-based systems extract and score candidates on meaning, letting recruiters assess large pools in days instead of weeks.

4

Generic outreach kills engagement

Identical messages sent to dozens of prospects get poor responses. Candidates now expect communication that recognises their specific skills and motivations.

5

Security and compliance are hard at scale

Applicant data spread across systems exposes sensitive information. Multi-tenant platforms must isolate each customer's data and enforce fine-grained access to meet privacy regulations.

The AI hiring pipeline

Job ad generation
Resume parsing
Semantic matching
Candidate ranking
Automated outreach
Recruiter review
Feedback loop — recruiter review feeds back into candidate ranking, so recruiter feedback improves future matches. The recruiter stays in control at the review step.
  • Job ad generation — a large language model drafts the role description.
  • Resume parsing — NLP extracts work history, education, and skills.
  • Semantic matching — vector embeddings and a skills knowledge graph match on meaning.
  • Candidate ranking — a hybrid ML engine scores and orders candidates.
  • Automated outreach — personalised messages drafted for recruiter approval.
  • Recruiter review — the human checkpoint; decisions feed back into ranking.

One continuous pipeline, from job ad to shortlist, that learns from every hiring decision.

Core platform capabilities

What our platform does, across the hiring lifecycle.

1

Automated job ad generation

A fine-tuned large language model creates polished, brand-aligned job descriptions in minutes, with bias-checked language. Recruiters give the role details; the model drafts the ad.

2

AI resume parsing and semantic matching

NLP and ML models extract work history, education, and skills from resumes, convert them into vector embeddings, and match them against job descriptions using a knowledge graph of skills and industries, so matching is based on meaning, not keywords.

3

Candidate ranking with continuous learning

A hybrid ranking engine combines semantic similarity with ML models (gradient boosting and transformer-based). Recruiter decisions (shortlist, interview, hire) feed back in, so recommendations sharpen over time.

4

Automated outreach and engagement

An AI assistant drafts personalised emails and LinkedIn messages using each candidate's skills, experience, and fit. Recruiters review before sending, so personalisation scales without extra workload.

5

Interactive candidate profiles

The platform can turn resumes into interactive video summaries, helping candidates tell their story and giving recruiters a better read on communication skills.

6

Multi-tenant SaaS with RBAC

Built for agencies and enterprises, it onboards multiple client organisations on shared infrastructure while keeping each tenant's data logically isolated. Role-based access control gives admins, recruiters, hiring managers, and analysts only the data their role needs.

7

Job board and ATS integration

Connects to ATS platforms like JobAdder and distribution tools like Idibu, so recruiters publish across Seek, LinkedIn, Indeed, and CareerOne, then receive applications back into the platform for processing.

8

Security and compliance

Sensitive data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and role-based permissions control who can view, edit, or export candidate information, enforcing least-privilege access.

Business impact and benefits

What an AI-first recruitment platform delivers. Where figures are industry research, they are attributed; the platform capabilities are ours.

Faster hiring and lower cost

Industry research on AI adoption in recruitment (the Unilever/IBM/Hilton studies) reported up to 85% less recruitment time, 30% lower hiring cost, and 16% better retention. Our platform is built to capture exactly these gains by automating the manual stages.

Higher recruiter productivity

LinkedIn reports 45% of recruiters using generative AI automate routine tasks and 41% see improved productivity. Our platform automates job-ad writing, screening, and outreach to the same end.

A personalised candidate experience

Automated outreach and interactive profiles give candidates a tailored, engaging experience, improving response rates and employer brand.

Better matching and diversity

Semantic search and knowledge-graph matching focus on skills and experience rather than keywords, reducing bias and improving match quality.

Secure collaboration at scale

Multi-tenancy and RBAC let organisations onboard many teams and external clients while keeping data separated, with the cost efficiency of shared infrastructure.

Conclusion

AI and automation are redefining recruitment: less manual work, better candidate-job matching, and a better experience for recruiters and applicants alike. Hiremii combines generative AI, semantic search, machine-learning ranking, and orchestration into one multi-tenant platform that scales with the business. By connecting directly to job boards and ATS platforms, it centralises hiring while keeping data secure and private. As AI adoption accelerates, the organisations that invest in automated, data-driven recruitment will hire faster, spend less, and compete harder for top talent.

Keylr — a flexible property-services marketplace

A UK property-services marketplace that connects property managers with vetted suppliers, built to close the communication gap and work fairly for both sides, with intelligent job dispatch, trust checks, negotiation, and full payments from quote to payout.

Two-sided (and multi-level) marketplace
Property managers, suppliers, and supplier subcontractors
Target-driven dispatch
Releases suppliers in batches until the PM’s quote target is met
UK trust checks
DBS, identity verification, and Checkatrade integration
Real-time chat + negotiation
Built to close the communication gap
Stripe Connect
Flexible payouts, refunds, and structured dispute handling

Introduction

Keylr is a UK property-services marketplace. Property managers post jobs; vetted suppliers quote and deliver them; and Keylr runs everything in between. The problem it was built to solve is the one that quietly breaks most property work: the communication gap. Jobs get lost in phone calls and emails, quotes are inconsistent, suppliers are overwhelmed or ignored, and neither side has a clear, shared view of what’s happening.

We built Keylr to fix that, on both sides of the marketplace at once. Property managers get control, trusted suppliers, and clean billing. Suppliers get a fair flow of relevant work and reliable payment. And both get real-time communication and negotiation in one place, so work gets agreed and done without the back-and-forth falling through the cracks. The hard engineering sits underneath: a target-driven dispatch algorithm, trust and compliance checks, a full payments and dispute layer, and infrastructure secure enough for identity and financial data.

The marketplace flow, end to end

Booked job cancelled — the engine auto-reroutes, finds replacement suppliers, and notifies the PM.
  • PM posts a job — service and postcode, quoted or fixed-price.
  • Target-driven dispatch — releases suppliers in batches until the PM’s quote target is met.
  • Suppliers quote — receive the job, chat, negotiate, and quote.
  • PM accepts — reviews and accepts up to their quote target.
  • Delivery & ticketing — job scheduled, delivered, and tracked to resolution.
  • Stripe Connect — handles payment from the PM and payout to the supplier.

From job posted to supplier paid, one controlled marketplace flow built around the PM’s quote target.

Solutions & impact

1

Target-driven batched dispatch

The challenge

For one service in one postcode there can be 100+ eligible suppliers. Notifying all of them at once floods suppliers, creates a race, and buries the property manager in quotes. But notifying too few risks the PM never getting enough quotes to choose from.

Our solution

A backend dispatch algorithm that works to a target. The property manager sets how many quotes they want, the target is dynamic, not fixed, so 10 is just an example. The engine sends the job to a first batch of around 20 relevant suppliers, ordered by service match, proximity, rating, and responsiveness. Because not every supplier in a batch will accept, the engine watches how many quotes come back, and only releases the next batch if the PM’s target hasn’t been met yet, until it is, then stops. Two safeguards keep the flow moving: if a notified supplier doesn’t respond within a set timeframe, the engine automatically drops them from the active list and pulls in the next best-fit supplier, so a slow supplier never stalls the job. And if a supplier cancels after a job has been booked and awarded, the algorithm automatically reroutes, finding and notifying replacement suppliers and alerting the property manager, so even the worst case is handled without manual chasing. It all runs asynchronously on the backend so it scales cleanly even in dense postcodes.

Impact

The property manager reliably gets the number of quotes they set, no more, no less, and the best-fit suppliers see the job first. Unresponsive suppliers are dropped automatically and replaced, and cancellations reroute on their own, so the job keeps moving without the PM chasing anyone. It’s a smarter middle ground than either blasting everyone or trickling out too few.

2

Closing the communication gap: real-time chat and price negotiation

The challenge

Most property work goes wrong in the gaps between messages, miscommunication on scope, price, and timing, spread across calls, texts, and email, with no shared record.

Our solution

Real-time chat is built directly into the job, so property managers and suppliers communicate in one place with a shared history. On top of that, a price negotiation tool lets the two sides agree a price within the platform rather than haggling offline, so the agreed scope and price are captured against the job.

Impact

Fewer misunderstandings, faster agreement, and a clear shared record of what was agreed, the communication gap the whole platform was built to close.

3

Trust, compliance, and refined supplier choice

The challenge

Suppliers enter tenants’ homes and handle property. A marketplace that can’t prove its suppliers are trustworthy is a legal and reputational liability, and property managers want to choose from genuinely vetted suppliers.

Our solution

Trust and compliance checks are built into supplier onboarding, including DBS background checks and identity verification, enforced before a supplier can accept work. Integration with Checkatrade gives property managers the flexibility to choose from more refined, independently vetted suppliers on top of Keylr’s own checks.

Impact

Property managers get suppliers they can trust in occupied homes, with the option to filter to Checkatrade-vetted suppliers, and the marketplace reduces its legal and reputational exposure by enforcing verification up front.

4

Flexible for both sides: teams, supplier companies, and subcontractors

The challenge

A rigid two-sided model doesn’t fit how property work really operates. Property managers work in teams; suppliers are often companies that pass work to their own subcontractors.

Our solution

Property managers can build a team inside the platform, so a group can manage properties and jobs together. On the supply side, supplier companies can onboard and then dispatch jobs to their own subcontractors, so Keylr supports a multi-level marketplace, not just a flat one-to-one match.

Impact

The model bends to how both sides actually work, PM teams collaborate, and supplier companies scale their own workforce through the platform, which widens supply and improves fit.

5

Quote control and fixed-price jobs

The challenge

In an open marketplace a property manager can lose control of how many suppliers they engage and how work is priced.

Our solution

Property managers set how many quotes they want to accept per job (the target that drives the dispatch engine), keeping them in control of choice. The platform also supports fixed-price jobs, where the price is set up front instead of quoted, for standardised or routine work.

Impact

Property managers stay in control of cost and choice, and both quoted and fixed-price work run through one consistent flow.

6

Tenant management and ticketing

The challenge

Work spans many properties, tenants, and jobs at once, and without one system it fragments across calls, emails, and spreadsheets.

Our solution

Integrated tenant management and a ticketing system track every job and issue from raised to resolved, giving property managers one place to manage properties, tenants, and the work across them, with a clear status trail on every ticket.

Impact

One operational source of truth, less manual coordination, and a visible audit trail on every job.

7

Payments, payouts, and dispute handling (Stripe Connect)

The challenge

A marketplace moving money between property managers and suppliers has to handle payouts, refunds, and disputes cleanly, or it drowns in reconciliation and legal risk.

Our solution

Full Stripe Connect integration handling the money end to end. Supplier payouts run on flexible schedules, fortnightly, monthly, or instant, with BACS and direct debit for UK payments. It includes structured dispute management, remedies, credit notes, and refunds, designed to resolve conflicts cleanly and reduce the risk of legal litigation. Every money movement is tracked and reconcilable.

Impact

Suppliers are paid reliably on the schedule that suits them; property managers get clean billing, refunds, and credit notes; and disputes run through a defined process that protects the marketplace legally. This is the CFO’s section: predictable cash flow, clean reconciliation, and reduced legal exposure.

8

Tiered, spend-based pricing with tracking

The challenge

Property managers who bring more volume expect to be rewarded, and they want to see where they stand.

Our solution

A tiered pricing engine where a property manager earns a discount once their spend passes defined thresholds, with tracking so they can see their spend and tier status in real time.

Impact

Higher-volume property managers are rewarded automatically, encouraging retention, and they get transparency into their spend instead of a black box.

Infrastructure & security

Keylr runs on hardened cloud infrastructure built for sensitive personal and financial data.

Private gateway and network isolation

Traffic routes through a private gateway, with services in private subnets and no direct public exposure of critical backend components.

End-to-end encryption

Data encrypted in transit and at rest.

Segmented access

Marketplace, trust, and payment layers isolated at the network level, so the most sensitive parts of the system are protected by design.

Infrastructure-level security, not just application-level, because the platform handles identity checks, home access, and money movement.

Secure infrastructure & payments

Trust checks, marketplace logic, negotiation, and payments, all inside a private, encrypted network.

Business impact

Marketplace & experience

Target-driven dispatch delivers the exact number of quotes the PM wants without spamming suppliers; real-time chat and negotiation close the communication gap; PM teams and supplier subcontracting make the model flexible for both sides.

Trust & compliance

DBS and ID verification enforced at onboarding, plus Checkatrade integration for refined supplier choice, reduce legal and reputational risk.

Financial

Stripe Connect handles flexible payouts (fortnightly, monthly, instant), BACS and direct debit, plus refunds, credit notes, and structured dispute remedies that reduce litigation risk; tiered spend-based pricing rewards volume.

Infrastructure

Private gateway, subnets, and end-to-end encryption protect sensitive identity and payment data at the infrastructure level.

Conclusion

Keylr is a full property-services marketplace, engineered where it’s genuinely hard. A target-driven dispatch algorithm gives property managers exactly the quotes they want without overwhelming suppliers. Real-time chat and in-platform negotiation close the communication gap the whole platform was built to solve. DBS, identity, and Checkatrade checks make suppliers safe to send into homes. A complete Stripe Connect layer handles flexible payouts and disputes cleanly enough to reduce legal risk. And PM teams and supplier subcontracting make the model flexible for how both sides really work. It’s a marketplace built to be fair to both parties, and to hold up commercially, legally, and operationally.

Taxionspot — a ride-hailing platform, rebuilt right

We inherited a taxi-booking platform mid-build, audited it, and found security flaws that were quietly costing the business money, on a product whose whole promise is a fixed price you can trust. We rewrote it, for web and mobile, into a secure, well-structured platform for booking, dispatch, and payments.

Next.jsReactReact NativeMySQL
Inherited mid-build
Taken over an in-progress project, then audited and rewritten
Critical flaw found
Customers could edit the fixed fare in the browser and pay less than the real price
Rewritten for web + mobile
A secure, well-structured platform on solid foundations (iOS + Android live)
Secrets secured
Credentials moved off the front end and out of the git history
Server-side validation
Prices and bookings verified on the backend, never trusted from the client

Introduction

Taxionspot is a licensed taxi service in Eindhoven, Netherlands, a 24/7 dispatch operation running airport transfers, business travel, group, medical and school transport across a mixed fleet, with one core promise to its customers: a fixed price you see upfront, no surprises. But Ellocent's story with it didn't start at a blank page. We were brought in when the project was already in progress, part-built by others, and asked to take it forward.

Whenever we inherit an in-progress project, we don't just carry on coding. We first audit what's already there, the coding standards, the structure, and, most importantly, the security. On Taxionspot, that audit found problems the client had no idea were there, including one that struck at the heart of their whole value proposition: the fixed price wasn't actually fixed. So rather than build on a weak foundation, we rewrote the software for both web and mobile: secure, well-structured, and built to scale. This is the story of what we found, and how we fixed it.

The price-tampering flaw, and the fix

Before — price trusted from the browser
Browser shows €100 fare
Customer edits value in inspector
Booking submitted at €10
Backend accepts it

The “fixed price” could be rewritten by the customer. The company was charged €10 for a €100 ride, and didn't notice.

After — price validated on the server
Browser requests a fare
Backend calculates & owns the real price
Customer can't change it
Booking confirmed at correct price

The price is decided and verified server-side. The browser can't override it.

Before: the browser set the price. After: the server owns it. The fix is architectural, the client is never trusted to set the price.

Solutions & impact

1

The critical flaw: the “fixed price” could be edited from the browser

The challenge / what we found

The web version let customers book a taxi, for example from Eindhoven Airport to their destination, at a fixed price shown upfront. But that price was calculated and trusted on the front end. Anyone could open the browser's inspect tool, change the displayed fare, and complete the booking at whatever amount they typed. A €100 airport ride could be booked for €10. On a business built entirely on a trustworthy fixed price, this was both a direct financial loss and a threat to the core promise, and the client hadn't noticed it until our audit surfaced it.

Our solution

We moved all pricing logic to the backend. The server now calculates and owns the real fare and validates every booking against it, so a price sent from the browser is never trusted. What the customer sees is display-only; what they're charged is decided server-side and cannot be tampered with.

Impact

The revenue leak was closed and the “fixed price” promise became real. Every booking is charged the correct, server-verified fare, and a whole class of front-end tampering is designed out.

2

Secrets exposed on the front end and in the git history

The challenge / what we found

During the audit we found sensitive credentials and secrets kept on the front end, and committed into the git repository, both serious exposures. Anyone with access to the client-side code or the repo history could have retrieved them.

Our solution

We moved all secrets off the front end into secure, server-side configuration, removed them from the codebase, and put proper secret management in place. Sensitive keys are no longer shipped to the browser or stored in version control.

Impact

A major exposure was closed. Credentials are protected, and the platform no longer leaks secrets through its front end or its git history.

3

Inheriting a project: auditing standards and structure first

The challenge

Taking over a part-built project is risky, you don't know what decisions were made, what corners were cut, or what's hiding in the code. Building further on a weak base only compounds the problem.

Our solution

Before writing new features, we ran a full audit of the inherited codebase, coding standards, architecture and structure, and security. This is our standard practice for any ongoing project we take on. The audit is what surfaced the pricing flaw and the exposed secrets, and it told us the foundation wasn't safe to build on.

Impact

The client got an honest, expert assessment of what they'd actually paid for so far, and a clear decision: rewrite on solid foundations rather than pile more work onto a flawed base.

4

Rewriting for web and mobile on solid foundations

The challenge

Once the audit showed the existing build couldn't be trusted, the platform needed to be rebuilt properly, for both web and mobile, without losing what the business needed it to do.

Our solution

We rewrote the software with clean structure and secure-by-default practices across a Next.js and React web app and a React Native mobile app (live on iOS and Android), on a MySQL backend. Booking, dispatch, fleet, and payment logic were rebuilt so the critical decisions (pricing, validation, secrets) live on the server where they belong.

Impact

A secure, well-structured, maintainable platform across web and mobile, built to scale with the business instead of accumulating hidden risk.

5

Real-time booking, dispatch, and a mixed fleet

The challenge

Coordinating real-time booking and dispatch across a mixed fleet, standard sedans, a Tesla Model Y electric option, comfort cars, and vans for up to 8, with fixed-price quoting per vehicle class, live tracking, and accurate ETAs, is genuinely complex, especially 24/7 and at peak.

Our solution

We built real-time booking and dispatch with vehicle-class-aware fixed pricing, live driver tracking, and ETA estimation, so riders book, see the fixed price per vehicle type, and track their ride, and the right vehicle is matched to each job. Average pickup in Eindhoven is around 8 minutes.

Impact

Reliable real-time booking and tracking across the whole fleet, with the correct fixed price shown per vehicle class and accurate ETAs, day and night.

6

Secure, flexible payments

The challenge

Supporting cash, card in the car, and in-app payment means integrating payments securely and scalably, exactly the area where the inherited build had already gone wrong.

Our solution

We rebuilt the payment flow with secure, server-validated integrations, so every transaction is verified on the backend against the correct fixed fare, across all payment methods.

Impact

Flexible payment options for riders, with the security and integrity the original build lacked.

Security: our standard for every project

The Taxionspot rescue reflects how we work on every engagement, and especially on projects we inherit. The flaws we found here are exactly the kind our process is designed to catch.

We audit inherited projects first

Standards, structure, and security, reviewed before we build anything new.

We never trust the client

Prices, permissions, and critical decisions are validated on the server, never taken on trust from the browser or app.

Secrets stay out of the front end and version control

Credentials live in secure server-side configuration, not in client code or git history.

We build secure by default

Security isn't a phase at the end, it's how the software is structured from the start.

Who it serves

Passengers

Quick, convenient rides with a trustworthy fixed price, flexible payment, and ~8-minute average pickup.

Business clients

Punctual, professional transport for guests and staff.

Medical & school transport

Safe, on-time rides to appointments and school.

Group travellers

Vans for up to 8 people, travelling together.

Drivers

Reliable bookings and easy management of rides, schedules, and payments.

Admins

Full backend control of fleet, bookings, and payments.

Impacts & benefits

Revenue leak closed

Server-side fare validation stopped the browser price-tampering that was costing the business on real bookings, and made the “fixed price” promise real.

Secrets secured

Credentials moved off the front end and out of git history.

A trustworthy foundation

A full rewrite on clean, secure, well-structured code across web and mobile, live on iOS and Android.

Secure by default

Critical logic validated server-side, never trusted from the client.

Reliable operations

Real-time booking, dispatch, and tracking across a mixed fleet, 24/7.

Flexible, secure payments

Cash, card, and in-app, verified on the backend.

Conclusion

Taxionspot is the kind of project that shows what an engineering audit is really worth. We inherited it mid-build, and before adding a single feature we checked its standards, structure, and security, the way we do with every ongoing project. That audit found a flaw that let customers rewrite their own fare in the browser, booking a €100 ride for €10, on a business whose entire promise is a fixed price you can trust, along with secrets exposed on the front end and in the git history. Rather than build on that, we rewrote the platform for web and mobile: secure by default, with pricing and validation owned by the server, secrets kept where they belong, and clean structure built to last. The client didn't just get a finished app. They got the one they thought they already had.

Relait — AI & automation in investor relations

Turning investor relations from slow, manual, reactive work into intelligent, proactive engagement, powered by AI and automation.

Introduction

Investor relations keeps getting harder. Shareholder bases are larger, reporting deadlines are tighter, and the regulations are stricter. Yet most of the work, collecting data, drafting reports, formatting documents, coordinating communications, is still slow, manual, and scattered across tools. It’s a function under growing pressure, running on processes that were never built to scale.

We built an AI-powered platform that automates and connects those workflows, turning investor relations into something faster, more scalable, and fully compliant. With it, reports are produced 70% faster, disclosures are drafted in minutes with no compliance delay, communications are personalised to lift engagement, operations scale to handle up to five times more investors with no extra headcount, and every workflow stays audit-ready.

From weeks of manual, sequential work to days of automated, validated delivery.

Solutions & impact

Here’s how the platform transformed each part of investor relations, with the results it delivered.

1

Streamlining reporting cycles: from weeks to days

The problem

Quarterly and annual reports are cornerstone communications, but they traditionally take 3–4 weeks of intensive work. Data extraction, table building, narrative drafting, and formatting all happen in sequence, by hand, and each step invites delays and version conflicts. Reviews across finance, legal, and communications stretch the timeline further.

Impact
  • Report generation time cut by roughly 70%.
  • IR teams shifted their effort from formatting to analysis, adding more value.
  • Version control tightened and error rates dropped sharply through automation.
Our solution
  • Data integration — API connectors ingest transactional and financial data straight from source systems, removing manual exports.
  • AI-driven drafting — A natural language generation engine, trained on historical reports and the company’s tone guidelines, drafts disclosures automatically.
  • Human-in-the-loop validation — Analysts review the AI drafts, focusing on strategic insight and accuracy rather than formatting.
  • Automated publishing — Once approved, the system packages reports into PDF and web-ready HTML and distributes them across investor portals and regulatory channels.
2

Accelerating market announcements under compliance pressure

The problem

Timely announcements are critical, but legal and compliance review cycles hold them back. Drafting a disclosure can take hours of back-and-forth, and social and email updates often trail the official exchange filing, leaving communication gaps.

Impact
  • Disclosure drafting cut from hours to minutes.
  • The lag between official filings and investor communications eliminated.
  • Manual compliance errors reduced through AI validation.
Our solution
  • Generative AI drafting — Domain-specific language models draft compliant disclosures aligned with ASX and NYSE frameworks in minutes.
  • Pre-submission validation — AI modules cross-check each disclosure against exchange rules and flag compliance issues before submission.
  • Multi-channel automation — Once approved, announcements publish simultaneously to exchange platforms, investor portals, email lists, and social channels.
3

Enhancing investor engagement through personalisation

The problem

Traditional IR relies on mass emails with generic messaging and little feedback on engagement. Social updates are reactive, often posted late, and miss the window on investor sentiment.

Impact
  • A significant lift in email engagement.
  • Communications became targeted and relevant instead of generic.
  • Faster, data-informed adjustments to messaging.
Our solution
  • Segmented AI personalisation — AI analyses investor profiles and segments audiences to tailor subject lines, executive summaries, and key insights.
  • Real-time engagement analytics — Dashboards show live open rates, click-throughs, and sentiment, so communication can be adjusted on the fly.
  • Automated social snippets — Social posts are generated from announcements and published instantly to keep market presence current.
4

Ensuring compliance and auditability

The problem

Compliance checks and audit trails are usually manual, line-by-line, with approvals tracked across emails and spreadsheets. That raises risk and makes audits painful.

Impact
  • Compliance risk substantially reduced through automated rule enforcement.
  • Audit readiness improved with transparent, complete documentation.
  • Administrative overhead cut for IR and legal teams.
Our solution
  • AI compliance validation — Automated checks against regulatory requirements flag issues before submission.
  • Role-based approval workflows — Digital workflows enforce approvals by role, preventing unauthorised submissions.
  • Immutable audit logs — Every draft, edit, and approval is recorded in tamper-proof logs, giving a complete audit trail.
5

Scaling investor relations with shareholder growth

The problem

As shareholder numbers grow, inquiries and communications grow with them. Scaling the old way means hiring proportionally more people, driving up cost and complexity.

Impact
  • IR teams handle up to 5x the investor volume with no headcount increase.
  • Leadership gets early-warning indicators for proactive risk management.
  • Investor service improves with rapid, 24/7 chatbot responses.
Our solution
  • Predictive analytics — Machine learning analyses trading patterns and sentiment to flag potential sell-offs or reputational risks early.
  • Automated mass distribution — Email and social updates reach thousands of investors at once, with no manual effort.
  • AI-powered investor chatbots — Context-aware chatbots answer common questions, drawing on filings and historical Q&A.
6

Secure document management and controlled access

The problem

Investor communications involve sensitive financial disclosures that demand strict security, precise version control, and controlled access. Manual handling across scattered storage raises the risk of leaks, version drift, and compliance lapses.

Impact
  • Sensitive shareholder data protected even inside the organisation, not just from outside threats.
  • Stronger data security and lower risk of unauthorised disclosure.
  • Greater investor confidence through reliable, controlled access.
  • Simpler audits, backed by complete, tamper-proof version histories.
Our solution
  • Encrypted cloud repositories — Secure cloud storage with end-to-end encryption protects data at rest and in transit.
  • Data masking and tokenisation — Sensitive fields such as shareholder identifiers, holdings, and personal details are masked or tokenised, so they’re never exposed in logs, non-production environments, or to users without explicit clearance. The real values stay encrypted; everyone else sees only what their role permits.
  • Role-based access control — Access to disclosures and reports is controlled by role (investors, analysts, legal), so people see only what they’re authorised to.
  • Automated versioning — Every document version is saved and tracked, giving an immutable history for audits.
  • Investor portals — Secure, easy-to-use portals let investors access current disclosures on demand, reducing ad hoc inquiries.
7

Continuous investor communication and feedback

The problem

IR is increasingly expected to be an ongoing dialogue, not a periodic broadcast. The traditional approach has no mechanism for real-time feedback or sentiment analysis, so investor concerns go unaddressed and messaging can’t adapt.

Impact
  • IR shifted from a one-way channel into a responsive, two-way engagement platform.
  • Higher investor trust and satisfaction, with concerns addressed in near real-time.
  • Leadership gained actionable insight into sentiment trends to inform strategy.
Our solution
  • Interactive investor portals — Two-way portals let investors submit questions, browse FAQs, and get real-time updates beyond static reports.
  • AI-powered feedback analysis — NLP aggregates and analyses investor queries, sentiment, and engagement to surface emerging concerns.
  • Proactive alerts and dashboards — Real-time dashboards and alerts turn investor sentiment into actionable insight for timely responses.

Why this matters: the strategic shift

Bringing AI and automation into IR is more than a technology upgrade. It changes the nature of the function.

ManualMachine-driven

Repetitive, time-consuming tasks are automated, freeing human expertise for strategy.

ReactiveProactive

Real-time data and alerts enable anticipatory communication and risk mitigation.

GenericPersonalised

Communications become targeted and relevant, building engagement and trust.

FragileScalable

The system absorbs growth without operational bottlenecks.

Conclusion

This platform is Ellocent Labs’ engineering vision for investor relations as a future-ready discipline, powered by AI and automation. By pairing machine-driven efficiency with human oversight, it delivers compliance assurance, rapid execution, and tailored investor engagement at scale.

  • Report timelines cut from weeks to days.
  • Disclosures validated and published within minutes.
  • Personalised communication that resonates across investor segments.

EternaDx — a precision- longevity platform

A platform that cross-references genetics, proteomics, blood analytics, and wearable data into one clear, personalised picture of your biology, and turns raw data into non-diagnostic, actionable insight.

4 data types

Compliance and quality standards

Introduction

Wearables have made biological data abundant and meaningless at the same time. A watch shows steps, sleep, and heart rate, thousands of data points with no clinical context, so people are measured more than ever but understand themselves no better. EternaDx set out to fix that by doing something much harder than tracking: interpretation.

EternaDx cross-references four very different sources, a person's genetics (700,000+ markers), proteomics, blood analytics, and continuous wearable data, into one coherent picture of what's happening in their body, and what they can do about it, as non-diagnostic, personalised guidance. The engineering challenge sits underneath: ingesting and normalising radically different data types, turning 692,000 polymorphisms into a readable report, syncing continuous streams from seven-plus wearable ecosystems, handling deeply sensitive health data to GDPR standard, and running the whole commercial layer of kits, subscriptions, and add-ons. That's what we built.

Four data sources, one interpretation

Genetics

Proteomics
blood / epigenetic

The value isn't any one data source, it's cross-referencing all four into meaning
  • Four inputs — genetics, proteomics, blood analytics, and continuous wearable data.
  • Ingestion & normalisation — radically different formats unified into one biological profile.
  • Interpretation engine — cross-references all four; OpenAI / Flowise render readable, non-diagnostic output.
  • Report & recommendations — structured guidance across sport, nutrition, prevention, longevity, and social.
  • User — one clear, personalised picture in the app dashboard.

Genetics, proteomics, analytics, and wearables, cross-referenced into one clear, personalised picture. These are wellness and personal-knowledge insights, not a medical diagnosis.

Solutions & impact

1

Cross-referencing for incompatible data types

The challenge

Genetics, proteomics, blood analytics, and wearable data are completely different in format, cadence, and meaning, static genetic markers, periodic lab results, and continuous real-time streams. Making them speak to each other, so an insight can draw on all four at once, is the central engineering problem.

Our solution

A data model and ingestion pipeline that normalises each source into a unified biological profile, so the interpretation layer can reason across genetics, proteins, analytics, and wearable signals together rather than in isolation.

Impact

A single, coherent view of a person's biology instead of four disconnected data silos, the thing wearable apps alone can't do.

2

Turning 692,000 polymorphisms into a report a person can actually read

The challenge

A genetic test analyses 692,000+ polymorphisms. Raw genetic data is meaningless to a non-expert, the challenge is turning that volume into a clear, structured, personalised report without losing scientific rigour.

Our solution

An interpretation and reporting engine that distils the genetic analysis into structured sections (Sport, Nutrition, Prevention, Longevity, Social), each with overall scores and detailed marker-level breakdowns, and uses AI (OpenAI / Flowise) to render clear, personalised, non-diagnostic explanations of what each marker means and what to consider.

Impact

Users get a readable, interactive, lifelong genetic report from an enormous dataset, clear enough to act on, rigorous enough to trust.

3

Real-time wearable integration across many ecosystems

The challenge

Users bring whatever device they already own, Garmin, Fitbit, Oura, Polar, Withings, Apple Health, Health Connect, each with its own API, data model, and quirks. Continuous biometric streams have to be ingested reliably from all of them.

Our solution

Integrations across 7+ wearable ecosystems that pull activity, sleep, and heart-rate data into the platform continuously, normalise it, and feed it into the same interpretation engine as the genetic and lab data, giving the “real context” a raw wearable app can't.

Impact

Whatever device a user owns, their live biometric data becomes part of one interpreted picture, not another isolated app.

4

Home-collection and lab workflow

The challenge

The product runs on physical samples, saliva kits and dried-blood-spot tests, shipped to homes, returned to a lab, processed, and delivered back as digital results, a logistics-plus-software workflow that has to stay reliable and traceable.

Our solution

A workflow connecting kit ordering and shipping, sample tracking, lab processing timelines (results in defined windows), and digital delivery of the finished report into the app, so the physical and digital halves stay in sync.

Impact

A smooth path from “order a kit” to “read your results in the app,” with the lab workflow handled behind the scenes.

5

Handling deeply sensitive health data

The challenge

Genetic and proteomic data is among the most sensitive personal data that exists. Protecting it to GDPR standard, encrypted and access-controlled, is non-negotiable.

Our solution

The platform is built to GDPR compliance, with health data encrypted and protected, and access controlled, in line with the medical-device quality standards the product operates under (ISO 13485, ISO 9001, CE-marked IVD).

Impact

Users trust the platform with their most sensitive data, because privacy and security are built in, not bolted on.

6

The commercial platform: kits, subscriptions, and add-ons

The challenge

The business runs on several revenue models at once, one-off genetic-test kits, multi-kit family packs, a monthly/annual Pro subscription, optional blood-analysis add-ons, and a waitlist with paid reservations for a premium test. That's a non-trivial payments and entitlement problem.

Our solution

A Stripe-based commercial layer handling one-off kit purchases, tiered packs, recurring Pro subscriptions (monthly and annual), optional add-ons, and waitlist reservations with deferred remaining payment, with platform access and entitlements tied to what each user has bought.

Impact

Multiple revenue streams run cleanly through one system, and users move from purchase to platform access without friction.

Architecture & tech

Built on Java and FastAPI services with a PostgreSQL data layer and a Next.js/TypeScript front end. AI interpretation uses OpenAI and Flowise to turn complex biological data into clear, personalised, non-diagnostic explanations. Payments and subscriptions run on Stripe. Wearable integrations span Garmin, Fitbit, Oura, Polar, Withings, Apple Health, and Health Connect.

A simple four-step journey over a complex genetics, lab, and wearable pipeline.

Impacts & benefits

From data to meaning

Cross-referencing four data types turns disconnected metrics into one interpreted picture, the core value wearables alone can't deliver.

Readable at scale

692,000+ polymorphisms distilled into a clear, interactive, lifelong report.

Device-agnostic

7+ wearable integrations, so users bring whatever they already own.

Privacy by design

GDPR-compliant handling of highly sensitive genetic and health data.

Multiple revenue streams, one system

Kits, packs, subscriptions, add-ons, and reservations run cleanly through a unified Stripe layer.

Scale

74,500+ people already measuring their biology on the platform.

Conclusion

EternaDx shows what it takes to turn abundant biological data into genuine understanding. The hard part was never collecting data, it was cross-referencing genetics, proteomics, analytics, and wearables into one coherent, readable, non-diagnostic picture, reliably and privately, at scale. By engineering the data integration, the interpretation and reporting pipeline, the multi-ecosystem wearable sync, the kit-and-lab workflow, and a clean multi-model commercial layer, we helped build a platform that gives tens of thousands of people real answers about their biology, with their most sensitive data protected throughout.

Introduction

Renting is full of friction, and most of it comes down to three things: people can't communicate cleanly, landlords guess at the right price, and creating a good listing is slow, manual work. Tolobi was built to take all three off the table.

It connects landlords, tenants, guests, and roommates on one platform, then uses AI to do the parts people find hardest: writing the listing, recommending the right properties to each tenant, and suggesting a market-accurate price for the landlord's specific area. Real-time chat keeps owners and tenants talking in one place with a shared history, and a flexible role-and-permission system lets each type of user do exactly what they should. The result is a rental experience with less guesswork, less manual effort, and far fewer of the communication breakdowns that usually derail a rental.

How a property goes from empty to rented

Landlord adds a property
Generates listing contentAI

Three AI touchpoints — content generation, price suggestion, and recommendations — do the heavy lifting
  • Landlord adds a property — core details in; no copywriting required.
  • AI listing content — a polished, consistent listing is generated automatically.
  • AI price suggestion — a market-accurate price for the landlord's specific area.
  • AI recommendations — the listing is surfaced to the tenants most likely to rent it.
  • Real-time chat — owner and tenant talk in one place with a shared history.
  • Booking — the match turns into a booking.

From an empty property to a rented one, with AI handling the listing, the pricing, and the match.

Solutions & impact

1

AI-generated listings and content

The challenge

Writing a good property listing is slow and inconsistent. Landlords either spend real time crafting descriptions or post thin, low-quality listings that don't attract tenants, and quality varies wildly across a platform.

Our solution

Automatic property listing with AI-based content generation. A landlord provides the core property details, and the platform generates a polished, consistent listing, description and supporting content, ready to publish. It turns a manual writing task into a few clicks.

Impact

Listings go live faster, read consistently well across the whole platform, and landlords spend their time on decisions instead of copywriting.

2

AI market-price suggestions by area

The challenge

Landlords routinely mis-price. Too high and the property sits empty; too low and they leave money on the table. Most don't have reliable, local pricing data to work from.

Our solution

An AI-based pricing engine that suggests a market-accurate price for the landlord's specific area, so pricing is grounded in the local market rather than guesswork. The landlord stays in control and can adjust, but starts from an informed number.

Impact

Properties are priced to rent, reducing empty periods and under-pricing, giving landlords a data-backed starting point instead of a guess. This is the landlord's commercial win, and a CFO-style outcome: better yield and less vacancy.

3

AI-based property recommendations

The challenge

Tenants scroll through irrelevant listings and miss the ones that actually fit, and good matches for a landlord's property go unseen. Generic search alone doesn't surface the right match.

Our solution

AI-based recommendations that surface the right properties to the right tenants, based on their preferences and behaviour, so tenants see relevant options first and landlords' properties reach the people most likely to rent them.

Impact

Faster, better matches on both sides, tenants find suitable homes sooner, and landlords fill properties with less effort.

4

Closing the communication gap: real-time owner–tenant chat

The challenge

Rental deals stall and sour in the communication gaps, questions unanswered, details lost across calls, texts, and email, with no shared record and no privacy.

Our solution

Real-time chat built directly into the platform, so owners and tenants communicate in one place with a shared history. To protect privacy, in-platform email is handled through Mailslurp, which generates a dedicated email account per user, with custom webhooks forwarding and threading messages, so people can correspond without exposing personal email addresses, and the full reply chain is preserved.

Impact

Fewer misunderstandings, faster responses, and a clear, private, shared record of every conversation, the communication friction the platform was built to remove.

5

Flexible, permission-based access for every kind of user

The challenge

Landlords, tenants, guests, roommates, and admins all need very different views and powers, and screen access and data had to be generated dynamically from each user's permissions. Handling the complex many-to-many relationships between roles, permissions, and users, cleanly across every module, was the core engineering challenge.

Our solution

A fine-grained, permission-based role system that renders screens and data dynamically per user, so each role, landlord, tenant, guest, roommate, admin, sees exactly what it should, and the system scales as roles and modules grow.

Impact

One platform serves five very different user types safely, with clean access control that scales as the platform expands.

6

Frictionless guest access

The challenge

Forcing people to register before they can even look drives them away, but capturing interested visitors matters.

Our solution

A guest experience with a pre-viewing questionnaire and search filters that lets visitors browse and enquire about properties without registering, capturing their details so they can convert to a full account and booking later.

Impact

The platform stays open to everyone, more visitors engage, and interested guests are captured for conversion instead of lost at a signup wall.

Conclusion

Tolobi set out to take the friction out of renting, and it did it by putting AI where the manual pain was. AI generates the listing and its content, suggests a market-accurate price for the landlord's area, and recommends the right properties to the right tenants, while real-time chat and private in-platform messaging close the communication gap that usually derails a rental. Underneath, a flexible role-and-permission system serves landlords, tenants, guests, roommates, and admins from one platform. The result is a rental experience that's faster to list, smarter to price, easier to match, and far less manual, for everyone involved.

Skylark — real-time control, smarter logistics

One dashboard for end-to-end, real-time control of fleets, loads, and drivers. We replaced a patchwork of disconnected tools and spreadsheets with a single multi-tenant platform for delivery tracking, route optimisation, live telematics, and proof of delivery from the field.

React NativeNext.jsPythonFastAPISelenium

Introduction

Skylark was trying to run a modern logistics business on tools that didn’t talk to each other. Telematics ran through Trimble, which the team found complex, limited, and costly. Messaging lived in another system. Different operations were spread across separate tools, Workwave Optimo, CloudHawk, and Rider among them, each solving one slice of the job. And underneath it all, the real coordination, which drivers were free, which loads to allocate, which trailer went where, was managed by hand in Excel.

That patchwork was expensive, hard to learn, limited, and dangerously error-prone, one wrong cell in a spreadsheet could cost real money. Ellocent replaced the whole thing with a single application: a real-time logistics control tower that runs inbound and outbound loads, driver allocation and tracking, live telematics, and proof of delivery from one dashboard, built multi-tenant so it serves Skylark and its partner companies together. Skylark isn’t just software for them now, it’s their logistics control tower.

From a patchwork of tools and spreadsheets to one real-time logistics control tower.

Solutions & impact

1

Consolidating a patchwork of disconnected tools

The challenge

Skylark ran daily operations across several systems, Trimble for telematics (complex, limited, and costly), a separate messaging tool, and others like Workwave Optimo, CloudHawk, and Rider for different operations. Every tool meant another licence, another login, another data silo.

Our solution

We built a single platform that brings all of these operations into one dashboard, so the team runs the business from one place instead of switching between systems. We integrated the capabilities worth keeping and replaced the tools that were redundant or overpriced.

Impact

One system instead of many, far less complexity, and no more data stranded in silos, and by removing the licensing sprawl, total operations cost fell from over $30k to about $5k a month.

2

Replacing spreadsheet dispatch with a real load planner

The challenge

The heart of the operation, finding free drivers, allocating jobs, and managing inbound and outbound loads, was run in Excel. As volume grew, that became slow, overwhelming, and fragile.

Our solution

We built inbound and outbound load management and a load planner module into the platform. Dispatchers plan and document loads electronically, see which drivers are free, and assign jobs directly, with the data live and shared instead of trapped in a spreadsheet.

Impact

Faster, clearer dispatch, a real-time view of drivers and loads, and an end to manual spreadsheet juggling that didn’t scale.

3

The cost of manual data

The challenge

Manual spreadsheets don’t just slow a team down, they invite expensive, hidden mistakes, and they hide them for days.

Our solution

Moving operations into a purpose-built system with structured inputs, validation, and real-time visibility, instead of free-form spreadsheet cells, designs out whole categories of manual error, and makes the state of every load and trailer visible to the team rather than buried in a file.

Impact

The kind of silent, costly mistake a spreadsheet allows, and hides for days, is engineered away. Errors are caught at entry, and nothing critical sits unnoticed in the yard.

The incident that made the case

A team member setting a trailer’s temperature by hand typed ‒50 instead of 50. The trailer sat in the yard for three days at the wrong setting. It was carrying paint, which froze and was ruined, a costly, avoidable loss from a single mistyped cell.

4

Real-time telematics and GPS (Samsara)

The challenge

Fleet telematics ran through Trimble, which the client found complex, limited, and expensive, and GPS visibility across trucks and trailers wasn’t unified with the rest of operations.

Our solution

We integrated Samsara directly into the platform, bringing live GPS and telematics from the trucks’ and trailers’ built-in systems into the same dashboard the team uses for dispatch and loads. Location and vehicle data sit alongside operational data, not in a separate tool.

Impact

Unified, real-time visibility of the whole fleet inside one platform, on modern telematics, without the cost and complexity of the old system.

5

A driver app with proof of delivery at the source

The challenge

Drivers needed a simple way to be tracked, receive jobs, and handle paperwork, proof of delivery and received documents, without friction on the road.

Our solution

We built a React Native driver app with live driver tracking and scan-based document upload. Drivers capture proof of delivery by scanning documents from their phone, and documents received during a job are scanned and uploaded too, flowing straight back into the system for the operations team to track in real time.

Impact

Proof of delivery and job documents are captured at the source and visible to the office instantly, no chasing paperwork, no lost documents, and a live view of every driver.

6

Real-time communication built into the workflow

The challenge

Messaging lived in a separate tool, and delays or miscommunication between drivers and dispatchers on the road caused missed deadlines and confusion.

Our solution

We built messaging directly into the platform, with real-time chat, custom chat groups for teams or topics, chat search, and dispatch-integrated chat so dispatchers assign deliveries inside the conversation without switching tabs.

Impact

Communication and operations live in one place, cutting the delays and miscommunication that used to come from juggling a separate messaging tool.

7

Multi-tenant architecture for partner companies

The challenge

Skylark works with partner companies (for example Transexpert and Prestige Freight LLC), some under partnership arrangements. A single-company tool couldn’t serve that structure cleanly.

Our solution

We built the platform multi-tenant, so Skylark and each partner company operate in their own space on the same system, with data appropriately separated, while shared, partnered operations still work together. Role-based permission control means each user sees only what they should.

Impact

One platform serves a group of related companies, each with its own operations and secure access, without standing up a separate system per company.

Tech & integrations

Consolidated or replaced: Trimble, a separate messaging tool, Workwave Optimo, CloudHawk, and Rider.

Cloud infrastructure & security

The platform runs on AWS in the Canada region, so operational and fleet data stays resident in Canada, and it was engineered so consolidating the old patchwork also removed the licensing overhead that was expensive and hard to manage. Running trucks, trailers, drivers, and partner companies on shared cloud infrastructure, rather than a stack of separately licensed tools, is what took total operations cost from over $30k a month to around $5k, while adding, not sacrificing, security.

AWS Canada region

Hosted in AWS’s Canada region for data residency, low-latency access for North American operations, and managed, elastic infrastructure that scales with fleet volume.

Network isolation

Services run in private subnets with no direct public exposure; traffic routes through controlled gateways, keeping the operational core off the open internet.

End-to-end encryption

Fleet, load, driver, and document data is encrypted in transit and at rest, including scanned proof-of-delivery and job documents flowing in from the driver app.

Role-based access control

Fine-grained, least-privilege permissions per user and per tenant, so Skylark and each partner company reach only their own data.

Multi-tenant isolation

Each partner company operates in its own logically isolated space on shared infrastructure, so one platform serves the whole group without data crossing between tenants.

Continuous monitoring

Live system monitoring and alerting across the cloud environment, so issues surface and are acted on in real time rather than discovered later.

The commercial case: $30k+ to $5k a month

Every replaced tool, Trimble telematics, the separate messaging system, Workwave Optimo, CloudHawk, and Rider, carried its own licence, and those fees were a constant overhead that was hard to track and manage. Consolidating everything onto one platform on AWS Canada removed that licensing sprawl entirely. Total monthly operations cost, cloud infrastructure included, fell from over $30,000 to roughly $5,000, while the platform now runs 500 trucks and trailers across Skylark and its partner companies on secure, encrypted, data-resident infrastructure.

Impacts & benefits

One platform, not many

Operations run from a single dashboard instead of a patchwork of tools.

Lower cost and complexity

Replacing multiple licensed tools (including costly, complex telematics) cuts spend and the learning curve.

Fewer costly errors

Structured, validated inputs replace free-form spreadsheets, designing out the kind of manual mistake that once froze a trailer of paint for three days.

Real-time fleet visibility

Samsara telematics and GPS unified with dispatch and loads.

Paperwork solved at the source

Drivers scan proof of delivery and documents from the app; the office tracks them live.

Faster dispatch decisions

Real-time monitoring and live updates let dispatchers react quickly.

Built for the group

Multi-tenant architecture serves Skylark and its partner companies together.

Conclusion

Skylark’s operation was held together by too many tools and too much manual work, expensive, complex, and fragile, where one mistyped spreadsheet cell could freeze a trailer of paint for three days. Ellocent replaced the patchwork with one purpose-built, multi-tenant platform: inbound and outbound loads, driver allocation and tracking, Samsara telematics and GPS, in-built communication, and a driver app that captures proof of delivery at the source, all in one dashboard, for Skylark and its partner companies together. Many disconnected systems became one, and an operation run on spreadsheets became a real-time logistics control tower, running 500 trucks and trailers across Skylark and its partner companies on secure, encrypted AWS Canada infrastructure, at roughly $5,000 a month instead of the $30,000-plus the old licensed patchwork cost.
